title: Functions Scaling and Hosting Plans
description: Compare Consumption, Premium, and Dedicated hosting plans and understand how Azure Functions scales automatically.

data.text: Azure Functions runs on one of three hosting plans. Each plan has different scaling behavior, cost structure, and feature availability.

cards.title: Premium Plan
cards.description: Pre-warmed instances with no cold starts and VNet support.
cons: Requires at least one pre-warmed instance

cards.title: Dedicated (App Service)
cards.description: Runs on an App Service plan with fixed capacity.

data.text: On the Consumption plan, Azure adds new function instances automatically when the number of incoming events increases. Each instance processes one event at a time. When traffic drops, instances are removed.

data.caption: Consumption plan auto-scaling behavior
data.definition:
graph TB
    A[Incoming Events] --> B{Queue Depth > Threshold?}
    B -->|Yes| C[Add Function Instance]
    B -->|No| D[Keep Current Instances]
    C --> E[Process Events]
    E --> F{Queue Empty?}
    F -->|Yes| G[Remove Instance]
    F -->|No| E

data.title: When to Choose Premium
data.text: Choose the Premium plan when you need consistent low latency (no cold starts), VNet access, or longer execution times. It is the right choice for production APIs.

data.title: Azure CLI — Create a Premium Function App
data.content:
az functionapp create \
  --resource-group myResourceGroup \
  --consumption-plan-location eastus \
  --runtime dotnet-isolated \
  --functions-version 4 \
  --name myPremiumFuncApp \
  --storage-account mystorageaccount \
  --plan MyPremiumPlan

data.title: Explore Scaling Behavior
data.description: Deploy a function on the Consumption plan and observe how it scales under load.
steps: Deploy an HTTP-triggered function to the Consumption plan
Use a load testing tool to send 100 concurrent requests
Monitor the 'Current Scale' metric in the Azure portal
Observe how instances increase with load
data.expectedOutcome: You will see the number of instances increase automatically during the load test.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Consumption: pay-per-use, auto-scales to zero, cold starts
Premium: pre-warmed, no cold starts, VNet support
Dedicated: fixed capacity, App Service plan
Choose Premium for production APIs requiring low latency
data.takeaway: Pick the hosting plan based on your latency, cost, and networking requirements.
